headline: FaceID co-inventor raises $52M for AI brain health analysis to diagnose cognitive disorders
summary: Gidi Littwin, co-inventor of Apple's FaceID, has raised $52 million for Hemispheric, his startup developing an AI to decode brain activity. The goal is to non-invasively diagnose cognitive disorders like PTSD and Alzheimer's.
details: Gidi Littwin, co-inventor of Apple's FaceID and Vision Pro technology, has secured $52 million in funding for his startup, Hemispheric. The company is building a frontier AI model to decode electrical activity in the brain, aiming to diagnose cognitive disorders without invasive procedures.

Littwin left Apple in 2020 and partnered with Hagai Lalazar, who had begun developing AI for brain study. Littwin's experience with massive data collection for FaceID and Vision Pro was crucial for Hemispheric's data strategy.

Traditionally, diagnosing conditions like depression, Alzheimer's, and Parkinson's relies heavily on subjective questionnaires and behavioral observations. Hemispheric addresses this by collecting extensive objective brain data.

The startup gathered a quarter of a million hours of brain data from 100,000 paid volunteers across Asia, Tel Aviv, and Boston. This data trained a deep learning model to infer brain function from electrical activity, similar to how large language models deduce meaning from text.

Hemispheric tested its generalized model on subsets of people, including those diagnosed with PTSD, schizophrenia, and depression, reporting accurate deductions about their brain health. The team is now conducting a clinical study to test the model's ability to diagnose and predict Alzheimer's.

Their first product, designed for PTSD study, will be submitted to the FDA for approval early next year, with a public rollout hoped for by late 2027. The vision is for this technology to be as accessible as a blood test, used in clinics and psychologists' offices.

Patients would wear a lightweight EEG headset for about 15 minutes, interacting with a tablet app. The AI model would then assist clinicians in decoding signals, making diagnoses, predicting treatment effectiveness, and monitoring patient progress.

The $52 million funding will be used to advance partnerships with governments, healthcare organizations, and pharmaceutical firms, expand hiring in the US, and pursue regulatory approval. Hemispheric also plans to collect brain data from millions more people to further refine their AI model.

headline_marked: [[Palit officially announces RTX 3060 return]] with 12GB VRAM, a 2021 GPU revived for AI demand
headline: Palit officially announces RTX 3060 return with 12GB VRAM, a 2021 GPU revived for AI demand
summary: Palit officially joins Gigabyte and Manli in relaunching the 2021 RTX 3060 with 12GB VRAM, a move by Nvidia to combat GPU scarcity caused by the AI boom.
details: Nvidia's RTX 3060, a graphics card originally released in 2021, is being relaunched to combat component scarcity driven by the AI boom. Palit has officially announced its RTX 3060 Infinity 2 OC, joining other manufacturers like Gigabyte and Manli in bringing back the Ampere-generation GPU.

The new/old card features identical specifications to the original RTX 3060, including 3,584 CUDA cores and 12GB of GDDR6 VRAM on a 192-bit bus. Palit's overclocked variant boosts up to 1,792 MHz, a minor increase over Nvidia's mandated boost clock.

The PC hardware industry has faced turbulence due to the AI boom, which has led to production inadequacies and skyrocketing prices for silicon. With Nvidia's latest Blackwell family using expensive GDDR7 memory and vendors prioritizing HBM for higher margins, reviving older cards became a creative solution.

Palit has not yet provided an official price for the Infinity 2 OC, but similar renewed RTX 3060 variants have been appearing around $329. While the RTX 3060 was well-regarded at its initial launch, consumers are advised to consider newer RTX 50-series or used RTX 40-series GPUs for better performance.

For instance, an RTX 5060 Ti is currently available for approximately $369, offering significantly faster performance and support for DLSS 4.5. Despite having 8GB of VRAM, the RTX 5060 Ti (and regular 5060) generally outperforms the RTX 3060 in most scenarios, especially below 4K resolutions.

From a manufacturing standpoint, rebooting the RTX 3060 is logical due to better yields from Samsung's older 8nm process compared to TSMC's more expensive N5 node used by Ada and Blackwell. However, for consumers, newer generations typically offer superior efficiency and features.
